name: TripoSplat
paper_title: Generative 3D Gaussians with Learned Density Control
license_interpretation: MIT is a permissive license, so the code and weights can be used in commercial and closed-source products; the only obligation is to keep the copyright and license notice with copies. LibreYOLO's adapter is MIT; the denoiser, octree and Gaussian decoders it ports from TripoSplat keep MIT, and the preprocessing and encoder tokenization shared with Speridlabs Idol come from the Apache-2.0 Idol SDK, with notices in libreyolo/models/gen/triposplat/NOTICE. The denoiser, decoder and BiRefNet weights are redistributed by LibreYOLO as LibreYOLO/LibreTripoSplat0.6b (MIT), byte-identical to VAST-AI/TripoSplat, and the FLUX.2 VAE downloads from black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-4B (Apache-2.0). The DINOv3 image encoder is the exception: it is Meta's, under the DINOv3 License, a custom agreement that is not OSI-approved. It permits redistribution with a copy of the agreement and passes through trade-control and end-use restrictions (military, weapons, espionage and nuclear uses among them). LibreYOLO mirrors that encoder in bfloat16 at LibreYOLO/LibreDINOv3vith16plus together with the agreement, so nothing is gated; read the agreement before shipping a product on it.
